data_window: GitHub Search API queries for AI agent, LLM app, RAG, MCP, browser agent, code agent, voice agent, workflow, copilot, and assistant repositories created or pushed from 2026-09-04 through 2026-09-06. Raw search snapshots were saved under /tmp/radar_2026_09_06_api/; selected repository metadata, root-content and README audits were saved under /tmp/radar_2026_09_06_readmes/.
source_summary: Queried 10 GitHub Search API surfaces and deduplicated 268 repositories. Reviewed metadata, topics, root files, README headings, package/Docker/test clues, install paths, demos/screenshots and runtime claims for 29 shortlisted repositories. No third-party repository was cloned, installed, built, executed, browser-tested, mobile-tested, provider-tested, credential-tested, payment-tested, safety-tested, or deployed locally.
trend_observations: Agent operations infrastructure dominated this window: memory, harness routing, model gateways, multi-agent terminals and agent workspaces all frame the agent as a long-running worker that needs state, logs, approvals and recovery. Browser/desktop control is moving toward governed computers with Dockerized workspaces, action records and human takeover. Voice and mobile companions are becoming control surfaces for agent presence rather than novelty chat add-ons. Strong runnability signals were Dockerfiles, package workspaces, CLI folders, examples, screenshots/demo GIFs, test directories, env templates and explicit quick-start sections.
assumptions: Scores are based on GitHub API metadata and README/root-content evidence collected on 2026-09-06, not local runtime proof. Star/fork counts are raw GitHub API values at collection time; no authenticated star-delta or traffic API was used. Repositories with suspiciously inflated counts, broad marketing claims, pure skill/prompt content, research benchmarks or mature category-incumbent status were downgraded or skipped even when active.
markdown_report: Top focus for 2026-09-06: agent memory infrastructure, parallel coding-agent ADEs, AI gateways, self-hosted personal agents, macOS terminal workspaces, governed browser computers, coding-agent configuration, realtime voice runtime, multi-agent workflow studios, and unified harness APIs. Watchlist covers agentic browsers, browser automation, local Agent OS, assistant home infrastructure, auditable headless browsers, job application agents, and mobile coding-agent companions. Skip reasons cover suspiciously inflated counts, mature incumbents, canonical vendor products, narrow MCP/devtools infrastructure, skill packages, benchmarks, and README-heavy marketing surfaces.

top_projects.audience: Developers who run multiple coding agents and need persistent context without rebuilding project memory every session.
top_projects.ai_native_angle: Memory is treated as portable agent infrastructure, with plugin surfaces for several agent runtimes and explicit session-to-session recall.
top_projects.growth_signal: Created 2025-08-31, pushed 2026-09-06; GitHub API showed 93,300 stars and 8,194 forks at collection time; README/root audit found plugin folders, CLI/MCP clues, SQLite/RAG topics, changelog, security docs and installer paths.
top_projects.runnability: High from README/root evidence: package files, plugin directories, installer docs and multiple host integrations are present, but no local install was attempted.
top_projects.recommended_action: Audit the memory data model and plugin boundary; compare against the radar automation memory pattern.
